guarantees.claim: endian_swap is always equal to cfg_reg.endian_swap.q.
digest_swap is always equal to cfg_reg.digest_swap.q.
key_swap is always equal to cfg_reg.key_swap.q.
hw2reg.cfg.hmac_en.d is always equal to cfg_reg.hmac_en.q.
hw2reg.cfg.sha_en.d is always equal to cfg_reg.sha_en.q.
hw2reg.cfg.digest_size.d is a type‑cast copy of digest_size, treated as digest_mode_e.
hw2reg.cfg.key_length.d is a type‑cast copy of key_length, treated as key_length_e.
hw2reg.cfg.endian_swap.d is always equal to cfg_reg.endian_swap.q.
hw2reg.cfg.digest_swap.d is always equal to cfg_reg.digest_swap.q.
hw2reg.cfg.key_swap.d is always equal to cfg_reg.key_swap.q.
reg_hash_start is asserted when both reg2hw.cmd.hash_start.qe and .q are high, else 0.
reg_hash_stop is asserted when both reg2hw.cmd.hash_stop.qe and .q are high, else 0.
reg_hash_continue is asserted when both reg2hw.cmd.hash_continue.qe and .q are high, else 0.
reg_hash_process is asserted when both reg2hw.cmd.hash_process.qe and .q are high, else 0.
hw2reg.err_code.de receives err_valid, enabling error-code capture.
hw2reg.err_code.d receives the current err_code value whenever de is active.
hash_start is high only when (reg_hash_start is high) AND (sha_en is high) AND (cfg_block is low) AND (invalid_config is low).
hash_continue is high only when (reg_hash_continue is high) AND (sha_en is high) AND (cfg_block is low) AND (invalid_config is low).
hash_process is high only when (reg_hash_process is high) AND (sha_en is high) AND (cfg_block is high) AND (invalid_config is low).
hash_start_or_continue is the logical OR of hash_start and hash_continue.

assumptions.claim: digest_size is a valid member of digest_mode_e, and key_length is a valid member of key_length_e.
assumptions.cond: when this chunk casts those values to the respective enum types (lines 342-343)
assumptions.risk: an out-of-range value produces an illegal enum encoding, potentially causing width mismatches, decode errors, or security bypass in downstream digest/key handling.

assumptions.claim: When err_valid is asserted, err_code holds a stable, correct error identifier.
assumptions.cond: during any cycle where err_valid is high (lines 354-355)
assumptions.risk: if err_code changes while err_valid is high, the hw2reg.err_code register may capture a transient or incorrect code, leading to inaccurate error reporting and weakened fault observability.

assumptions.claim: The signals sha_en, cfg_block, and invalid_config are stable during the active pulse of reg_hash_start/continue/process.
assumptions.cond: while any command-derived pulse (reg_hash_start, reg_hash_continue, reg_hash_process) is high
assumptions.risk: a mid-pulse change on these qualifiers can glitch the final hash_start/hash_continue/hash_process signals, causing incomplete or spurious control actions in the HMAC core.

assumptions.claim: The reg2hw command interface delivers qe pulses that are exactly aligned with stable, mutually exclusive (or intentionally combined) command bits.
assumptions.cond: when any of the hash_command qe signals is asserted
assumptions.risk: spurious or overlapping qe assertions can cause multiple reg_hash_* pulses simultaneously, which downstream may not handle safely.

uncertain_points.claim: hw2reg.err_code.de is driven continuously by err_valid, allowing the error code register to be updated every cycle while err_valid is high. If err_valid remains asserted and err_code changes, the first error code may be overwritten before software reads it.
uncertain_points.cond: err_valid = 1, err_code changes to a different value
uncertain_points.risk: first-fault information may be lost, undermining error containment and diagnostic accuracy.

uncertain_points.claim: The RTL provides no mutual exclusion among the four command pulses (reg_hash_start, reg_hash_stop, reg_hash_continue, reg_hash_process). If the register interface asserts more than one bit simultaneously, multiple control signals (hash_start, hash_continue, hash_process) may become active at the same time.
uncertain_points.cond: more than one cmd hash_* bit set in the same cycle
uncertain_points.risk: downstream HMAC logic may receive conflicting triggers, causing undefined state transitions or data corruption.

uncertain_points.claim: digest_size and key_length are cast to enum types digest_mode_e and key_length_e without range checking. An unsupported value will produce an illegal enum encoding that downstream width‑sensitive logic may misinterpret.
uncertain_points.cond: digest_size or key_length set to an unsupported/invalid code
uncertain_points.risk: can lead to incorrect digest size or key length interpretation, potentially compromising HMAC security and data integrity.
